newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Two Russians in Soyuz spacecraft undock from Mir.
newsitem.headline: Two Russians in Soyuz spacecraft undock from Mir.

text.p: A Soyuz spacecraft with two Russian cosmonauts undocked from the troubled Mir space station on Thursday to take them to Earth after the most gruelling mission in the programme's 11-year history.
Live television pictures at Mission Control showed Soyuz with commander Vasily Tsibliyev and flight engineer Alexander Lazutkin departing from Mir at 12:56 p.m. Moscow time (0856 GMT).
There appeared to be a three-minute delay in the operation compared to the original schedule but a Mission Control operator said the undocking went well.
"Everything is all right with you," the operator told the crew. "Thank God," responded Tsibliyev.

Along with British-born NASA astronaut Michael Foale, who will stay aboard Mir until next month, they have endured a series of major woes since they came aboard in February. The most serious was a June 25 collision between Mir and its resupply ship, the worst incident in Mir's history.
The station has run on partial power since then.
After the June collision, Tsibliyev began suffering heart irregularities which doctors said were stress-related.
He was given medication that has since been discontinued, and was not taking special medicine for the return trip, a mission medical adviser said.
Seconds before the undocking, Tsibliyev said: "Poor Mike must be worrying."
The initial speed of the the departing Soyuz was three metres (yards) per second.
A huge screen at Mission Control showed two bright dots -- Mir and Soyuz quickly departing from each other. "It seems we are quite far from it (Mir)," Tsibliyev said.
The crew is scheduled to touch down at 1216 GMT in the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan.
